A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TropNNC by the same authors. All pages, including appendices, are readable and support comparison. The substantial restructuring can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V2 reports original network-compression experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, and ImageNet, including accuracy and compression results in Tables 1–7 and Figures 7–9.

after.justification: V3 retains original compression experiments across these datasets and reports an additional iterative-versus-non-iterative comparison in Table 4.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain their core clustering, representative construction, and alternating minimization. V3 adds applied heuristics that normalize clustering inputs and exclude bias from clustering while retaining original weights for representative construction. These are explicitly used in CUP comparisons; v2 only discussed related normalization alternatives without recommending them.

E1.justification: V2's binary MNIST tasks distinguishing 3 versus 5 and 4 versus 9 disappear, including Tables 1–2. Multiclass MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, and ImageNet remain, with no new dataset or application domain.

E2.justification: Removing the binary-MNIST experiments eliminates the evaluated Zonotope K-means baseline. Neural Path K-means, ThiNet, CUP, random pruning, and L1 pruning remain in corresponding comparisons. Non-iterative TropNNC comparison curves also disappear from retained CNN plots. Newly cited methods such as SPvR are not evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 Figures 4–5 report three-iteration TropNNC where v2 Figures 7–8 often reported the non-iterative configuration. Non-uniform pruning thresholds change substantially, including VGG thresholds from 0.006/0.0085/0.011 to 0.014/0.017/0.02. ResNet56 and non-ReLU LeNet configurations disappear. The new Table 4 ablation uses different thresholds to obtain approximately matched compression budgets.

E4.justification: V2's non-ReLU robustness study in Figure 9 and its batch-normalization fusion comparisons and sensitivity observations are removed. V3 adds a non-uniform VGG ablation of iterative refinement in Table 4 and a worked failure example motivating bias suppression in the appendix. This substantially changes the supplementary evidence and questions examined.

E5.justification: V2 displays uncertainty values and error bars without explaining their construction. V3 Section 6 specifies averages over five experimental repetitions and standard-deviation error bars, and discloses selecting the best of five randomized compressions per model. These are reporting additions; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V3 Table 1 reproduces v2 Table 3, but several other tables and curves are removed or replaced, and an ablation table is added. The VGG result of 93.21% at 3.53M parameters becomes 91.71% at 2.75M under a different threshold (v2 Table 5; v3 Table 2). ImageNet/ResNet18 original accuracy changes from 70.10% to 69.75% (v2 Table 7; v3 Table 3). These changes do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The central Hausdorff bound, compression guarantees, and principal proof arguments are retained after renumbering and relocation. V3's appendix adds an explicitly unproved upper-hull Hausdorff bound and a construction demonstrating unbounded approximation error from an unsuitable clustering. V2's explicit examples contrasting discrete and continuous Hausdorff distances are omitted.

C1.justification: The main data-free compression and comparative-performance contributions remain. V3 drops v2's claim of being significantly easier to implement and calls its theoretical bound the 'tightest known,' whereas v2 claimed a tighter bound than previous work. These are limited changes to the contribution claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of directional clustering and why suppressing bias can preserve unbounded linear regions, while explicitly qualifying these improvements as heuristic. Detailed batch-normalization and residual-block restrictions from v2 are reduced or omitted. Interpretations of the VGG–ResNet performance difference and the two non-uniform threshold variants remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents ThiNet's 5,000-sample choice and its tuning procedure, and explains how clustering heuristics leave representative calculations unchanged. Conversely, it removes v2's detailed fusion alternatives, distinction between fusion before compression and layer-by-layer fusion, and use of pre-fusion weights for clustering. Reproducibility documentation therefore gains some details and loses others.

R1.justification: V3 replaces broad coverage of tropical applications, unstructured pruning, quantization, and low-rank approximation with a focused structured-pruning discussion. It adds works including SPvR, CHIP, and Luo and Wu (2020), and explicitly positions TropNNC relative to global pruning strategies. The central relationships to Misiakos et al., ThiNet, and CUP remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively condensed and rewritten. Related work moves after the method, tropical background moves into the appendix, and the standalone extensions section is redistributed. The appendix gains heuristic explanations and reorganizes the retained proofs.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout, with substantially smaller experimental panels and rearranged tables. Background illustrations move to the appendix, plot legends and displayed method curves change, and v2 Figures 4 and 9 disappear. V3 adds the heuristic illustration in Figure 6 and the ablation table.

improvement.justification: V3 improves focus, explains the new heuristics, documents statistical reporting, and adds an iterative ablation. However, it removes direct single-output validation and fusion procedures and sensitivity evidence relevant to interpreting CUP comparisons. Retained results also change operating points without fully explaining all setting differences. These gains and losses leave the net effect on methodological transparency and evidential strength uncertain.
